body:
As of v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee], I cannot edit my main project's math shader include file in Godot with the editor's default message queue memory setting, because introducing an error while editing the shader include causes Godot to crash. I doubled `memory/limits/message_queue/max_size_mb` (32 to 64) to avoid the crash. But, this really shouldn't be necessary in the first place.

This is with all console output disabled and shader compilation off. The MRP would have to be expanded to trigger this.

I discovered the memory workaround by running the editor in the terminal, with `./Godot_v4.4-stable_linux.x86_64 --verbose`, which reveals the following error before the crash:

```txt
Failed method: EditorNode::_print_handler_impl. Message queue out of memory. Message queue out of memory. Try increasing 'memory/limits/message_queue/max_size_mb' in project settings.
TOTAL PAGES: 8192 (33554432 bytes).
```

That's 33.55 megabytes of worthless output hanging and crashing the editor.

We could write out shader errors to a temporary path on the filesystem, and only print the path to that file in output. The downside is that the error file won't be easily accessible on platforms like Android, iOS and Web.

I don't need or want 33.55 megabytes of data being written to disk on error either. Such an enormous amount of superfluous text is of no use and still impacts CPU performance. The file and line listed in errors is already enough, because the shader editor highlights errors when open anyway. So, my ideal solution (and the one implemented by [my PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103894)) is disabling printing shader contents to standard output by default and providing a setting to enable it (which I seriously wouldn't recommend anyone do).

My PR does not touch the far more reasonable error messages. Although, I would be interested in making an additional PR afterward that adds a setting to limit shader compilation error messages to one at a time, as it's easy to end up with hundreds of identical error messages due to shader includes multiplying them. The MRP in this issue's description prints 192 errors that are just 2 errors duplicated 96 times. That's 190 total duplicate errors that are doing nothing but wasting CPU cycles and output space. And, that's a trivial example; my main project is more complicated.

This is a constant issue for me as well (in 4.4.1 stable), and it's hardly specific to includes. It's just writing shaders in general. I don't need my output log getting filled with a copy of the entire shader script each time an error is found. I have to manually clear the Output Log every 2 minutes while writing a script, or else the editor crashes.

I would much rather the editor simply highlight the lines with errors. For now I've had to just write new code inside of comment blocks, until I feel it's done, then uncomment to check it for errors. However, that's not really a solution if I have to give up most of the features that make using the editor appealing in the first place. At that point, using notepad++ to write everything seems more efficient.

Another alternative might be implementing an expandable error list like how the main code editor panel has at the bottom of the window? That would allow for placing all errors together in an organized list, and keeping them both compact and in a location that the user can see without having to switch tabs. As @OhiraKyou mentioned, the Shader Editor already highlights lines with errors. So the current behavior doesn't appear to be far off from the main code editor.

I'm surprised there aren't more responses to this issue, since I have the same problem regardless of project, project size, and any other factors. It simply comes down to script length and how long you've been working on it, how many times you pause mid-line (long enough to trigger compilation). With a sufficiently long enough script or combined includes, you could crash the editor with a single error just because you stopped typing to sneeze.

One last note: this does also highlight a difference in output log behavior between the main script editor and the shader editor, where the main editor does not include large swathes of code in error messages, only relevant lines. Bringing the behavior of the shader editor closer to that would also help streamline and increase parity of user experience between the two editor panels.

Yeah, I can only imagine that there just aren't many people writing substantial shader code, because the output becomes an obvious problem pretty quickly.

[My PR](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103894) disables the standard output of shader code (with a setting to enable it again), leaving just the error messages. The duplicate errors are still annoying, but it's a step forward.

I just started getting full editor crashes today while editing complex shader. I never had this with 4.3 stable.
This started happening in 4.4.1

I use only the shader editor to work on my shader code because toggling to another editor is not useful and i'd be hitting alt+tab hundreds if not thousands of times a day.

- My muscle memory of hitting Ctrl+S of saving a scene gives me a progress bar saying its saving the scene, which I *think* saves the shader file im editing.

- However, if I hit Ctrl+S to save a scene while I was editing a complex shader and its not finished compiling yet (sometimes they take a few seconds), and the editor tries to save a scene at the same time, the editor will crash and the line of shader code I was just typing in the editor is in lost.

- Pressing Ctrl+Alt+S while editing shader code gives no editor feedback it saved the shader file successfully.

I could work around a bunch of UX issues with the current shader editor if there is a way to turn off the shader editor trying to compile a shader while I am still typing code. 
**Please** let me just have a mode where it does not do this agggressive shader compilation while I am working on a shader, and let me just press Ctrl+Alt+S 'save file' (with some user feedback it saved the file also) to trigger a shader compile.

The lag and excessive editor log output issue gets even more problematic with editing .gdshaderinc files, if you stop typing or have a typo you'll trigger a ton of failed compilation issues that could have been avoided if I had some mechanism to stop shaders compiling that aren't ready to be.

- I have .gdshaderinc files that are shared between particle shaders, particle processing shaders, and material shaders applied to meshes, so its extremely painful to try and edit + use .gdshaderinc files with the current log output spam + autocompile functionality while using the builtin shader editor.


I am experiencing this issue on this editor version
Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads)

On a related note, there is no documentation about the 'Inspect Native Shader Code' option.
I click this option and the editor hangs for 15seconds or longer, becoming unresponsive and white-screens before becoming responsive again.

Is the editor default behavior trying to make 47 permutations of native shader code every time I edit+save a shader?
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee27e139-45b8-48d2-a3b5-35c1276c9a0f)
Is this part of the lag behind the scenes even if the source has a syntax error?

I went to project settings and just turned off the ShaderCache and this fixed a lot of lag and **MOST** of the full editor crashes I was regularly getting. If the shader cache really is doing a ton of work behind the scenes while authoring shaders and vfx I would like some control over when it decides to build that cache, otherwise i'll just workaround the issue and turn the shadercache off while using the editor.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53becbd8-ff50-42a7-9b95-d3087b9d59e2)

I am still getting regular crashes of the editor when editing shaders

Running console and verbose there is tons of this different error being thrown on successful editing and compilation of a shader *AFTER* there was a previous shader compilation failure due to a syntax error (due to the autosaving + shader compilation)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f10da03-a47e-41fd-914e-802150014f03)

I can then successfully edit a shader and iterate on it several times, and see this error thrown (as well as experience editor lag) and eventually the editor will crash.

I am able to leave the editor running overnight and there is no crash while running idle, the crash only happens when attempting to edit any shader and a recompile triggers, even on what would be a successful simple edit just changing a constant number.




Godot v4.5.dev4 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6094) - AMD Ryzen 9 3950X 16-Core Processor (32 threads)

This issue has been a major pain point for me.  I forked godot-engine, (https://github.com/dirk-arnholt/godot-gshade_fix), and merged PR's [#107547](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107547) and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103894, which fixes the issue for me.

Is there any way to escalate this issue to a maintainer that can merge fixes to master?  I really don't want to have to maintain my own fork.

This issue has been known for months, and is quite frankly catastrophic for developers who want to write non-trivial shader code.

I've also run into this issue.  I have a lot of shaders and shader includes, and if I edit an include in-editor, the whole editor will freeze up because it's printing out a massive shader (or multiple shaders) into rich text.  I have to edit shaders in an external editor so they won't try (and fail) to compile as I'm typing.

I also just ran into the editor freezing up for several minutes while doing an export.  After attaching a debugger, I discovered it was printing out shader code to the rich text log.  Not sure why, yet.  Still waiting for the editor to respond to see what the message is.  Logging in rich text is *very slow*.  Edit: Just remembered I enabled the shader pre-build/baking thing in 4.5, so that must be why it's generating all these errors.

Edit2: I think shader baker deadlocked, so I can't check to see what the log output was.  Seems to be forever waiting on tasks_mutex.
